title: Little Children
subtitle: The Letters of John in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
The letters of John were written by an old man to people he calls his little children. They begin with hands that touched the Word of life and a lamp with no darkness in it, and they keep circling back to the same few things: walk in the light, love one another, remain. Along the way: a basin of water for confession, a door shut against a neighbor in need, a love that casts out fear, a short note to a chosen lady, and a letter to Gaius about opening the gate for strangers.

This book walks through them in thirty-six short poems, in five parts: four for First John and one for the two short letters that follow it. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with the things the letters touch—a clay lamp, a loaf on a threshold, an ink pot set aside for the road—and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the letters of John alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

parts.title: Walk in the Light
parts.epigraph: God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.
parts.lightName: Light of Walk in the Light
parts.lightHint: Near 'what our hands touched' (1 John 1:1) in Part 1: Walk in the Light

parts.title: Little Children
parts.epigraph: Now, little children, remain in him
parts.lightHint: Near 'walk as he walked' (1 John 2:4–6) in Part 2: Little Children

parts.title: See How Great a Love
parts.epigraph: See how great a love the Father has given to us
parts.lightName: Light of See How Great a Love
parts.lightHint: Near 'called children' (1 John 3:1) in Part 3: See How Great a Love

parts.title: God Is Love
parts.epigraph: God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.
parts.lightHint: Near 'love is of God' (1 John 4:7–8) in Part 4: God Is Love

parts.title: Face to Face
parts.epigraph: I hope to come to you, and to speak face to face

paintings.title: what our hands touched
paintings.epigraph: “that which we saw, and our hands touched, concerning the W ord of life”
paintings.poem:
he doesn't start
with an argument.

he starts with his hands.

we heard him.
we saw him.
we touched him.

an old man
remembering the weight
of a shoulder,
the warmth of a palm
passing bread.

whatever else you doubt,
he wants you to know
this wasn't a rumor.

life had a body.
and he was there.

paintings.title: that our joy may be full
paintings.epigraph: “that you also may have fellowship with us.”
paintings.poem:
he writes
so there will be room
at the table
for you.

not a lecture.
an invitation.

and then he says
something surprising:

we write this
so our joy
will be full.

his joy isn't finished
until you're here.

paintings.title: no darkness at all
paintings.epigraph: “This is the message which we have heard from him and announce to you”
paintings.poem:
not mostly light.
not light
with a few dim corners
you'd rather not check.

light.
in him
no darkness at all.

nothing to hide from you.
no mood
you have to manage.

whatever you bring
into that room,
it will be seen.

and it will be
the kindest seeing
you have ever known.

paintings.title: in the light, together
paintings.epigraph: “if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another”
paintings.poem:
you would think
walking in the light
would mean walking alone,

each of us
with our own lamp,
our own clean record.

but he says
the light does something else.

it puts us
on the same road.

we see each other clearly,
scars and all,

and keep walking
side by side.

paintings.title: if we confess
paintings.epigraph: “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins”
paintings.poem:
pretending is tiring.

saying
i'm fine,
i'm clean,
there's nothing here.

confession
is setting the bag down.

and on the other side
is not a frown.

it is someone
faithful,
someone fair,

already reaching
for the water.

paintings.title: for the whole world
paintings.epigraph: “not for ours only, but also for the whole world.”
paintings.poem:
my little children,
don't sin.

but if you do,

someone stands up
for you.

and his mercy
isn't a small room
for the few
who got it right.

it goes out the door,
down the road,
past the last village
you can see.

the whole world.

paintings.title: walk as he walked
paintings.epigraph: “he who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked.”
paintings.poem:
it's easy
to say i know him.

words cost nothing.

but knowing someone
changes how you walk.

the roads he took.
the people he stopped for.
the pace he kept
with the slow ones.

you don't prove it
with your mouth.

you prove it
with your feet.

paintings.title: already shines
paintings.epigraph: “the darkness is passing away and the true light already shines.”
paintings.poem:
an old command:
love one another.

a new command:
love one another.

it is both,
the way sunrise
is the oldest thing
and new every day.

the dark hasn't gone yet.

but it's going.

look east.
the true light
already shines.

paintings.title: nothing to trip on
paintings.epigraph: “He who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no occasion for stumbling in him.”
paintings.poem:
hate
is walking a dark stairway
you think you know.

you don't.
you miss a step.
you don't even know
where you're going.

love
is a lamp on the step.

it won't carry you.
but you'll see the edge

and the next one,
and the one after that.

paintings.title: to every age
paintings.epigraph: “I write to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name’s sake.”
paintings.poem:
little children,
you are forgiven.

young men,
you are strong.
the word lives in you.

fathers,
you have known him
a long time.

he wrote to each of them
where they were,
by season,

as if to say
there's no stage of life
the letter isn't
addressed to.

paintings.title: passing away
paintings.epigraph: “The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever.”
paintings.poem:
the stalls fold up
at dusk.

the silks go back in boxes.
the crowd goes home.
tomorrow the prices change.

everything that glitters
is already
on its way out.

but the one
who does the will of God,

like the old olive
in the middle of the square,

stays.

paintings.title: the anointing
paintings.epigraph: “the anointing which you received from him remains in you”
paintings.poem:
there will always be voices
telling you
you've missed something.

a secret.
a better version.
a newer Jesus.

but you are not
empty-handed.

what you heard
from the beginning
is still in you,

like oil
soaked into the grain
of the wood.

it doesn't wash out.

paintings.title: remain
paintings.epigraph: “remain in him, that when he appears, we may have boldness”
paintings.poem:
remain.

not visit.
not drop in
when things are hard.

stay.
unpack.
keep the lamp lit.

so that when he comes
up the path,

you're not
scrambling for the key.

you're already home.

paintings.title: called children
paintings.epigraph: “that we should be called children of God!”
paintings.poem:
see.

he stops the letter
just to say it.

look at this love.

we are called
children of God.

and then,
as if he knew
you'd shrug it off
as a figure of speech,

he adds:

and we are.

paintings.title: not yet
paintings.epigraph: “It is not yet revealed what we will be”
paintings.poem:
you are not finished.

no one can see yet
what you will be.

not even you.

but this much is known:
when he appears,
we will see him
as he is.

and seeing him,
we will be
like him.

paintings.title: out of death into life
paintings.epigraph: “W e know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers.”
paintings.poem:
the oldest story
of two brothers
ends badly.

Cain looked at Abel
and couldn't stand
the good in him.

the message
from the beginning
is the other way around:

love one another.

and when you do,
you find out
you've already crossed over.

death behind you.
life ahead.

paintings.title: laid down
paintings.epigraph: “By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us.”
paintings.poem:
if you want to know
what love is,
don't look it up.

look at him.

he laid his life down
the way you'd lay down
a cloak
for someone cold.

not taken.
given.

and then John says,
quietly:

we can do that too.

paintings.title: the closed door
paintings.epigraph: “sees his brother in need, then closes his heart of compassion against him”
paintings.poem:
it doesn't take much.

you see him.
you have enough.
and something in you
swings shut.

no argument.
no cruelty.
just a door
quietly closing.

so leave it open.

a loaf on the step
is a small thing.

but that's where
the love of God
comes in.

paintings.title: in deed
paintings.epigraph: “let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.”
paintings.poem:
say it,
yes.

and then
knead the bread.

paintings.title: greater than our heart
paintings.epigraph: “God is greater than our heart, and knows all things.”
paintings.poem:
some nights
your heart is a judge
who never goes home.

it lists everything.
it says
you should know better.

John doesn't argue.
he just says:
God is greater.

he knows everything
your heart knows,
and more,

and he is still here.

paintings.title: greater is he
paintings.epigraph: “greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world.”
paintings.poem:
there are many voices,
he says.
test them.

does it say
he came
in real flesh?
then listen.

and don't be afraid
of how loud
the others are.

the room is large.
the dark is wide.

the lamp is small.

and the lamp
is winning.

paintings.title: love is of God
paintings.epigraph: “He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.”
paintings.poem:
love one another,
for love is of God.

it doesn't start
with us.

every kindness
that has ever reached you

came up
from the same well.

you can know a lot
about God
and not know him.

but whoever loves,

has tasted
the water.

paintings.title: not that we loved
paintings.epigraph: “In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us”
paintings.poem:
we didn't go looking.

we didn't
work our way up
to heaven's gate.

the gate came
to us.

he sent his Son
while we were still
looking the other way.

that's how you know
it's love:

it went first.

paintings.title: no one has seen
paintings.epigraph: “No one has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God remains in us”
paintings.poem:
no one has seen God.

not once.
not fully.

and yet.

a bowl passed
across a table.

a hand
on a tired shoulder.

when we love one another,
he stays with us,

and the unseen God
is almost
in plain sight.

paintings.title: no fear in love
paintings.epigraph: “There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear”
paintings.poem:
fear
keeps the shutters closed.

it waits for the knock.
it rehearses
what it will say.

love opens them.

not because
there's nothing out there.

because the one
who is coming
is the one
who loves you.

and you can't be
afraid of that
and held by it
at the same time.

paintings.title: first
paintings.epigraph: “W e love him, because he first loved us.”
paintings.poem:
the almond blooms
before the leaves.

love, too.

his came first.
ours is the answer.

paintings.title: the brother you have seen
paintings.epigraph: “he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?”
paintings.poem:
it's easier
to love God
than your neighbor.

God doesn't
chew too loud.
God never
borrowed your tools.

but John won't let it go.

the one you can see
is the test

for the one
you can't.

paintings.title: keep yourselves
paintings.epigraph: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.”
paintings.poem:
he has written it all down
so you can know.

not hope.
not guess.
know.

you have the Son.
you have life.

and then,
like a father
at the door,

one last thing:

little children,
don't let anything
take his place.

paintings.title: to the chosen lady
paintings.epigraph: “Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us”
paintings.poem:
the elder,
to the chosen lady
and her children.

a short letter.
a house church, perhaps.
a family.

he doesn't say much.

but he says
grace,
mercy,
peace,

and he says them
as a promise,
not a wish:

they will be with us.

paintings.title: walking in truth
paintings.epigraph: “I rejoice greatly that I have found some of your children walking in truth”
paintings.poem:
he heard about them.
some of her children,
walking in truth.

and it made his day.

then he asks again
for the oldest thing:

love one another.

nothing new.
just the path
you've always known,

walked
one more day.

paintings.title: remain in the teaching
paintings.epigraph: “He who remains in the teaching has both the Father and the Son.”
paintings.poem:
some went further,
they said.
past the teaching.

past the flesh
and the blood.

beyond.

but the path
doesn't get better
when you leave it.

stay on the worn stones.

the Father is there.
the Son is there.

you don't have to go
further than that.

paintings.title: paper and ink
paintings.epigraph: “I don’t want to do so with paper and ink”
paintings.poem:
there is so much
he could write.

he puts the pen down.

some things
don't fit on paper.

they need a room,
a table,
a face.

he would rather
pick up
his cloak.

paintings.title: as your soul prospers
paintings.epigraph: “I pray that you may prosper in all things and be healthy, even as your soul prospers.”
paintings.poem:
dear Gaius,

i hope you're well.
i hope your body
keeps up
with your soul.

such an ordinary prayer.

the kind you'd write
to anyone you love.

and there it is,
in the Bible,

telling you
God cares about that too.

paintings.title: no greater joy
paintings.epigraph: “I have no greater joy than this: to hear about my children walking in truth.”
paintings.poem:
not a big church.
not a famous name.

just news
arriving with a traveler:

they're still walking.

an old man
reads it
by the lamp.

there is no greater joy
than that.

paintings.title: strangers at the gate
paintings.epigraph: “you do a faithful work in whatever you accomplish for those who are brothers and strangers.”
paintings.poem:
Gaius opened the gate.

travelers he had never met,
going out for the Name,
taking nothing.

he fed them.
sent them on their way
well.

in the same church,
Diotrephes
wouldn't receive them.
he wanted to be first.

two houses.
two gates.

imitate the good,
John says.

leave the gate open.84

paintings.title: by name
paintings.epigraph: “Greet the friends by name.”
paintings.poem:
peace to you.

the friends
say hello.

greet them for me,
he writes,

by name.

not the church.
not everyone.

each one.

that's how the letters end.

the way love always
comes to you:

face to face,
and calling you
by your name.86
